task.title: Multi-date change analysis
task.text: Track land change through time with a science-ready baseline.

task.title: Heat, evapotranspiration, or drought
task.text: Use Landsat's thermal strengths for water and energy balance questions.

task.title: Fast-repeat monitoring
task.text: Watch vegetation, flooding, or disturbance with denser revisit timing.

task.title: Custom preprocessing research
task.text: Start closer to the calibrated source when you need full control.

scale.title: One scene or small area
scale.text: A smaller study area with manual or semi-manual analysis.

scale.title: Regional / multi-scene
scale.text: A larger workflow that benefits from consistent tiling and automation.

priority.title: Fastest path to analysis
priority.text: Prefer products that are already corrected and analysis-ready.

priority.title: Maximum preprocessing control
priority.text: Prefer flexible source data even if more setup is required.

time-series|single-scene|simplicity.why: You want science-ready optical data for multi-date comparison without doing your own atmospheric correction.
time-series|single-scene|simplicity.bestFor: Vegetation indices, land-cover change, flood comparison, disturbance mapping
time-series|single-scene|simplicity.tradeoff: You gain speed and consistency, but not the rawest level of preprocessing control.
time-series|single-scene|simplicity.nextStep: Start with Surface Reflectance and QA bands, then add Surface Temperature only if heat matters.
time-series|single-scene|simplicity.teachingTip: Have students calculate NDVI only after identifying clouds, water, and season. The index is a tool, not the whole interpretation.

time-series|regional|simplicity.why: Regional time-series work benefits from tiled, analysis-ready products built for repeat processing and pixel alignment.
time-series|regional|simplicity.bestFor: Automated monitoring, dashboards, regional land-change pipelines
time-series|regional|simplicity.tradeoff: Best for tiled operational workflows rather than casual one-off scene browsing.
time-series|regional|simplicity.nextStep: Use ARD if your geography is covered; otherwise use Collection 2 Surface Reflectance with a similar pipeline.
time-series|regional|simplicity.teachingTip: Emphasize pixel alignment and repeat processing: ARD is about reducing setup friction for time series.

time-series|single-scene|control.why: If you need to choose or test your own preprocessing chain, Level-1 keeps you closest to the calibrated source.
time-series|single-scene|control.bestFor: Method development, custom atmospheric correction, specialized retrieval experiments
time-series|single-scene|control.tradeoff: More flexibility means more work before analysis can begin.
time-series|single-scene|control.nextStep: Begin with Level-1 only if you know why the standard Level-2 products are not enough.
time-series|single-scene|control.teachingTip: Use this path to teach preprocessing choices, then compare results with Level-2 products.

time-series|regional|control.why: Large custom studies sometimes require a controlled processing chain across scenes and years.
time-series|regional|control.bestFor: Algorithm research, cross-sensor harmonization experiments, custom corrections
time-series|regional|control.tradeoff: Operational overhead is much higher than ARD or Surface Reflectance.
time-series|regional|control.nextStep: Only choose this path if methodological control is a core project requirement.
time-series|regional|control.teachingTip: Ask learners to write a reproducibility checklist before scaling custom preprocessing.

heat-water|single-scene|simplicity.why: Your main question is thermal, so the science product designed for land surface temperature is the most useful start.
heat-water|single-scene|simplicity.bestFor: Urban heat, drought, evapotranspiration support, irrigation and water-stress interpretation
heat-water|single-scene|simplicity.tradeoff: Thermal interpretation still benefits from combining with optical products.
heat-water|single-scene|simplicity.nextStep: Pair Surface Temperature with Surface Reflectance for the strongest environmental interpretation.
heat-water|single-scene|simplicity.teachingTip: Teach that thermal pixels need context: hot bare soil, roofs, dry vegetation, and recent burns can all produce high-temperature signals.

heat-water|regional|simplicity.product: Collection 2 Surface Temperature plus ARD / Surface Reflectance
heat-water|regional|simplicity.why: Regional heat and water studies usually need both thermal response and optical land-surface context.
heat-water|regional|simplicity.bestFor: Watershed heat mapping, agricultural water-use studies, urban heat-risk assessment
heat-water|regional|simplicity.tradeoff: You are now managing at least two linked product streams.
heat-water|regional|simplicity.nextStep: Use Surface Temperature for heat and Surface Reflectance or ARD for land condition and masking.
heat-water|regional|simplicity.teachingTip: Compare similar seasons and acquisition times so the lesson is about land condition rather than weather noise.

heat-water|single-scene|control.product: Collection 2 Level-1 with thermal-focused custom workflow
heat-water|single-scene|control.why: Choose this only if you need to test retrieval methods beyond the standard surface temperature product.
heat-water|single-scene|control.tradeoff: Most users do not need this complexity.
heat-water|single-scene|control.nextStep: Compare your custom result against the standard Surface Temperature product.
heat-water|single-scene|control.teachingTip: Make validation part of the lesson: a custom method should explain why it is better for the question.

heat-water|regional|control.why: This is for teams building bespoke temperature or energy-balance workflows at scale.
heat-water|regional|control.bestFor: Research programs with well-defined custom models
heat-water|regional|control.nextStep: Use only with a clear calibration and validation plan.
heat-water|regional|control.teachingTip: Have students identify auxiliary data needs before they touch code.

fast-monitoring|single-scene|simplicity.why: You need more frequent observations than Landsat alone can provide, and HLS is built exactly for that need.
fast-monitoring|single-scene|simplicity.bestFor: Crop condition, flooding, rapid disturbance, vegetation dynamics
fast-monitoring|single-scene|simplicity.tradeoff: You gain temporal density but move into a harmonized cross-mission product space rather than Landsat alone.
fast-monitoring|single-scene|simplicity.nextStep: Use HLS first, then pull original Landsat scenes if you need mission-specific follow-up.
fast-monitoring|single-scene|simplicity.teachingTip: Use HLS to show how harmonization helps when clouds or rapid change make a 16-day cadence too sparse.

fast-monitoring|regional|simplicity.why: High-temporal monitoring over large areas is where HLS shines.
fast-monitoring|regional|simplicity.bestFor: Regional crop systems, recurring floodplains, landscape disturbance alerts
fast-monitoring|regional|simplicity.tradeoff: Thermal capability is not the center of this workflow.
fast-monitoring|regional|simplicity.nextStep: Use HLS for the rapid optical timeline and add Landsat thermal products if heat matters.
fast-monitoring|regional|simplicity.teachingTip: Point out the tradeoff: denser optical revisit does not replace Landsat's thermal value.

fast-monitoring|single-scene|control.product: HLS plus original Landsat / Sentinel follow-up
fast-monitoring|single-scene|control.why: You want fast revisit but also the option to inspect source missions more directly.
fast-monitoring|single-scene|control.bestFor: Targeted event analysis with flexible follow-up
fast-monitoring|single-scene|control.tradeoff: You are balancing speed with deeper source-level interpretation.
fast-monitoring|single-scene|control.nextStep: Screen with HLS, then pull the source scene when you need custom analysis.
fast-monitoring|single-scene|control.teachingTip: This is a strong workflow for event triage: broad search first, source inspection second.

fast-monitoring|regional|control.why: This keeps the dense revisit advantage while preserving room for custom downstream modeling.
fast-monitoring|regional|control.bestFor: Regional monitoring systems and advanced classification pipelines
fast-monitoring|regional|control.tradeoff: More moving parts than using HLS out of the box.
fast-monitoring|regional|control.nextStep: Use HLS as the observation backbone and customize the analysis layer, not the ingestion layer first.
fast-monitoring|regional|control.teachingTip: Teach students to customize where it adds insight, not where official products already solved the hard part.

custom-prep|single-scene|simplicity.why: If preprocessing itself is the point, Level-1 is the natural entry point.
custom-prep|single-scene|simplicity.bestFor: Teaching, experimentation, and custom correction demos
custom-prep|single-scene|simplicity.tradeoff: Not the fastest route to environmental interpretation.
custom-prep|single-scene|simplicity.nextStep: Use Level-1 only when the preprocessing decisions are part of the lesson or method.
custom-prep|single-scene|simplicity.teachingTip: Good for demonstrating atmospheric correction, calibration, and metadata, but not for most beginner environmental questions.

custom-prep|regional|simplicity.why: Even if you want a simpler workflow, custom preprocessing at scale starts from Level-1.
custom-prep|regional|simplicity.tradeoff: High setup cost compared with ARD or Level-2 products.
custom-prep|regional|simplicity.nextStep: Prototype on a small subset before scaling out.
custom-prep|regional|simplicity.teachingTip: A small prototype should include cloudy, clear, bright, dark, water, and vegetation examples.

custom-prep|single-scene|control.why: This combination explicitly asks for maximum preprocessing control on a manageable scale.
custom-prep|single-scene|control.bestFor: Sensor-method training, custom atmospheric correction, experimental retrievals
custom-prep|single-scene|control.tradeoff: You must do more work before you can answer the environmental question.
custom-prep|single-scene|control.nextStep: Document your preprocessing assumptions carefully so results stay reproducible.
custom-prep|single-scene|control.teachingTip: Ask students to record every correction, mask, scale factor, and excluded pixel rule.

custom-prep|regional|control.product: Collection 2 Level-1 plus custom scaled pipeline
custom-prep|regional|control.why: This is the most flexible and most demanding option in the guide.
custom-prep|regional|control.bestFor: Serious method development and large custom research programs
custom-prep|regional|control.tradeoff: Highest burden for compute, QA, and reproducibility.
custom-prep|regional|control.nextStep: Treat this as an engineering project, not just a data download step.
custom-prep|regional|control.teachingTip: A serious custom pipeline needs provenance, QA, validation, and computing plans.
